title: Sticky Toffee Pudding
summary: A soft, dark date sponge baked in a square tin, soaked with hot toffee sauce made from butter, dark brown sugar and cream, and served warm.

ingredients.item: soft unsalted butter, for the tin
fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Soak the dates
steps.text: Put the chopped dates in the heatproof bowl, pour over the boiling water and stir in the bicarbonate. Leave for 15 min, then blend to a rough purée; the bicarbonate softens the skins and darkens the sponge.

steps.title: Make the batter
steps.text: Heat the oven to 175 °C (155 °C fan) and butter and line the tin. Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt together. Beat the 60 g butter with the 150 g sugar for 2-3 min until fluffy, then beat in the eggs one at a time and the vanilla. Fold in the flour and date purée just until no streaks remain, so the sponge stays tender.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Scrape the batter into the tin and bake for 30-35 min, until risen and springy and a skewer pushed into the centre comes out clean.

steps.title: Make the toffee sauce
steps.text: While it bakes, melt the 115 g butter with the 170 g sugar in the saucepan. Whisk in the cream and salt and simmer for 3-4 min until glossy and slightly thickened.

steps.title: Soak and serve
steps.text: Poke the hot sponge all over with the skewer, pour over a third of the sauce and leave for 10 min to soak in. Cut into 9 squares and serve warm with the rest of the hot sauce.

tips: A common mistake is overbaking, which dries the sponge; start checking at 30 min.
Medjool dates give the softest, richest result.
Make the sauce ahead and reheat until bubbling just before serving.
Serve with vanilla ice cream or a little extra cold cream.
safety: Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep the pudding and sauce covered in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat squares with some sauce in the microwave or a low oven until piping hot. The sponge freezes for up to 2 months.
